problem: The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=t{e}^{-t},$ where $t>0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10},$ where $t>0$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x.$

$t\in (${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of decreasing $x,$ then its velocity is negative. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10}) \\  & =\frac{6t-6}{2\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10}} \\  & =\frac{6(t-1)}{2\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10}} \\  & =\frac{3(t-1)}{\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10}}\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x$, we solve $v(t)<0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & <0 \\ \frac{3(t-1)}{\sqrt{3{t}^{2}-6t+10}} & <0 \\ 3(t-1) & <0 \\ t-1 & <0 \\ t & <1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving to the direction of decreasing $x$ is 

$$
t\in (0,1).
$$
